section_insight:
The dependency graph has two dominant hubs that account for most structural risk. streamlit/whoop/db.py is the single most central file by PageRank (0.0254, 3x the next node) with 59 incoming edges and zero outgoing — it is a pure sink that every page, API route, and analytics module leans on directly. This is appropriate for a data-access layer in a personal tool, but it has no test file in the graph, making it the highest-impact untested file in the codebase. Any schema or API change here ripples to ~30 direct callers simultaneously.

The second hub is apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts (PageRank 0.0086, 29 fan-in, 4 fan-out, instability 0.12). Nearly every API route and page imports it. Its low instability score means it is appropriately stable, and it has apps/web/src/lib/auth.test.ts present in the graph, so test coverage exists. However its betweenness of 0.0042 is the highest of any non-sink node, meaning it sits on the most shortest paths between modules — a breaking change here would disconnect more pairs of modules than any other file.

Third tier bottlenecks worth watching: apps/web/src/lib/db/connection.ts (17 fan-in, betweenness 0, instability 0) is a pure sink with no test file visible. apps/web/src/lib/db/integrations.ts (7 fan-in, betweenness 0.0015) is imported by auth, sync, token, webhook-handler, and two API routes — it is the chokepoint between OAuth tokens and the database layer.

No import cycles were detected (cycle_count: 0). This is the graph's strongest structural property and should be preserved.

High fan-out fragile files: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/sleep/page.tsx imports 26 modules — the highest fan-out in the codebase. It is a page component with instability 1.0, so this is structurally expected, but it will be sensitive to any change in the analytics or chart layers. apps/web/src/lib/coach/persistence.ts (5 fan-out, instability 0.83) is a library file, not a page — high fan-out at library level is more concerning because it increases the blast radius of internal refactors. It imports loop, prompts, tools, auth, and db.py with no fan-in from tests.

Files that are central but have no test coverage visible in the graph: streamlit/whoop/db.py (highest PageRank overall, no test node edges), apps/web/src/lib/db/connection.ts (17 fan-in, no test edges), apps/web/src/lib/coach/persistence.ts (imported by the chat API route, no test edges), apps/web/src/lib/sync.ts (betweenness 0.00115, instability 0.56, no test edges despite apps/web/src/lib/sync.test.ts appearing as an isolated node with no outgoing edges — the test file exists but imports nothing, suggesting it may be empty or a stub).

Recommended actions: (1) Add integration tests for streamlit/whoop/db.py — even a smoke test that validates schema shape would reduce the risk of the 59-importer blast radius. (2) Treat apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts as a protected file — its high betweenness means any interface change should be reviewed carefully and covered by its existing tests before merging. (3) Investigate apps/web/src/lib/sync.test.ts — it appears as an isolated node with no imports, suggesting the test file is either empty or not yet connected to the module under test. (4) Consider breaking apps/web/src/lib/coach/persistence.ts into smaller pieces; 5 imports at instability 0.83 with no test coverage is the riskiest library-layer file in the TypeScript codebase.
